<SCRATCHPAD_REASONING>
This is a significant development. Brad has confirmed that there are no available 30-minute slots for all four partners next week. My next step is to accept Brad's proposed plan of action. He has suggested searching for times that work for three of the four partners. This is a logical next step, as it allows us to identify the path of least resistance. By finding slots that only conflict with one person's schedule, we can then approach that person to see if they can move their existing appointment.

I will approve Brad's suggestion and ask him to proceed with the search. I'll ask him to provide me with the options he finds. Once I have those, I can then make a decision on how to proceed. It's also important to acknowledge that this might not work, and we may need to consider other options if the single partner with the conflict is unable to reschedule. However, for now, this is the most promising path forward.

I will use my first action to respond to Brad and my second action to end the session, so that he can proceed with his search as quickly as possible.Thanks for the thorough search and the update, Brad. I agree with your suggestion. Proposing a time that works for three of the four partners and asking one to reschedule is our best bet at this point.

Please go ahead and search for times that work for:
1.  Priya, Marcus, and David (but not Elena)
2.  Priya, Marcus, and Elena (but not David)

Let me know what you find, and we can decide on the best option to propose.
